title: vLLM: Request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision allows remote code execution
desc:
## Summary

An untrusted multimodal request can set `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision`. When vLLM serves a model whose Hugging Face processor uses dynamic `auto_map` code and the operator enabled `--trust-remote-code`, this request value reaches `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and selects the Python revision imported by Transformers.

This lets a client replace the operator-reviewed processor module with code from another revision of the same model repository. The operator-selected model/data `revision` remains pinned; only the executed processor code changes.

Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process. The PoC below demonstrates this with an import-time filesystem write. It is fully offline and does not require a GPU, model weights, or changes to a real Hub repository.

## Affected snapshot

- Repository: [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm)
- Verified commit: [`570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e)
- Verified with Transformers 5.15.0 and 5.16.1
- Affected release range has not been bisected

## Affected configuration

The vulnerable path exists when all of the following are true:

1. The served model's processor uses dynamic `auto_map.AutoProcessor` code.
2. The operator enabled `trust_remote_code`.
3. The server can fetch the request-selected revision, or it is already cached.
4. The attacker can create or otherwise control a revision in the served model repository. An example is a [Hugging Face community pull-request ref](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/repositories-pull-requests-discussions#where-in-the-git-repo-are-changes-stored) when that repository permits them.
5. A multimodal request reaches the processor path.

The default `trust_remote_code=False` configuration is not affected.

## Attack surface

`mm_processor_kwargs` is accepted directly by public request models:

- [`TokenizeChatRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/protocol.py#L111-L114)
- [`ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L372-L375)

`/tokenize` is particularly relevant because vLLM's authentication middleware guards only `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, and `/cohere` prefixes:

- [`AuthenticationMiddleware`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py#L11-L62)

Consequently, `/tokenize` remains unauthenticated even when `--api-key` is configured, unless an external proxy protects it. The vLLM [Security Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/security/#unprotected-endpoints-no-api-key-required) documents `/tokenize` as an unprotected endpoint.

## Root cause

The request value follows this path:

1. [`OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L406-L435) places request `mm_processor_kwargs` in prompt extras.
2. Multimodal rendering forwards those kwargs into processor construction through [`MMProcessorInputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L751-L760) and [`_process_multimodal_async`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L831-L847).
3. [`MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/config/multimodal.py#L506-L518) overlays inference values on startup values, so the request wins.
4. [`cached_get_processor_without_dynamic_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L344-L375) filters only recognized processor-call keys. `code_revision` is retained as a processor-construction kwarg.
5. [`cached_processor_from_config`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L380-L390) pins `revision` and `trust_remote_code`, but forwards the remaining kwargs without reserving `code_revision`.
6. [`get_processor`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L205-L245) calls `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(..., revision=revision, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, **kwargs)`.
7. Transformers [`AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/models/auto/processing_auto.py#L294-L302) uses `code_revision` to retrieve and import the dynamic module through [`get_class_from_dynamic_module`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py#L474-L575), then removes it before loading processor data. This is why code comes from the attacker revision while configuration/data remain operator-pinned.

Request-time processor arguments are not separated from processor-construction arguments, and `code_revision` is not reserved.

## Suggested remediation

1. Separate processor-construction arguments from untrusted processor-call arguments. An allowlist of supported request-time preprocessing controls is safest.
2. Reject `code_revision` and other loader/source controls in request `mm_processor_kwargs`, and pass `model_config.code_revision` explicitly as the only permitted processor-code revision.
3. Add a regression test proving a request cannot change the loaded module revision while operator pins remain effective.
4. Protect `/tokenize` with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.

Expected safe behavior is either a 4xx response for reserved request keys or silently ignoring them before processor construction. Rejection is preferable because it makes attempted misuse visible.

A patch for this was merged here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830

title: qs : qs.stringify with arrayFormat 'comma' throws an uncaught TypeError on array elements carrying a non-callable own toString (DoS)
desc:
## Summary

`qs.stringify(obj, { arrayFormat: 'comma' })` throws an uncaught `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` when an array in `obj` contains an element that carries an own, non-callable `toString` property (for example `{ a: [ { toString: 'x' } ] }`). A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can influence an object that the application later re-serializes with the comma array format triggers the throw. In a service that lacks a synchronous error boundary around the serialization call, the uncaught exception crashes the worker process, producing a denial of service.

## Root Cause

When `arrayFormat: 'comma'` is selected, the comma branch collapses the whole array into a single value via `Array.prototype.join`, or, under `encodeValuesOnly: true`, maps each element through the value encoder before joining. Both paths perform an implicit string coercion (`ToPrimitive` with hint `"string"`) on each element. For an object whose own `toString` is a non-callable value, coercion skips the shadowed non-callable `toString`, falls through to `Object.prototype.valueOf` (which returns the object rather than a primitive), and throws. The comma branch runs this coercion before the per-element null and skip handling in the main loop, so nothing downstream can neutralize the hostile element, and the throw is never caught inside the library.

```text
lib/stringify.js  (comma-array branch)
  line 152-154: obj = utils.maybeMap(obj, function (v) { return v == null ? v : encoder(v); });  // encodeValuesOnly path
  line 156:     objKeys = [{ value: obj.length > 0 ? obj.join(',') || null : void undefined }];   // default comma path
lib/utils.js
  line 292:     string = String(str);   // value encoder coercion reached via the encodeValuesOnly path
```

## Impact

Prerequisites: the application calls `qs.stringify` with `arrayFormat: 'comma'` (a documented, supported option) on an object whose shape can be influenced by attacker input. Attacker-controllable sources include `qs.parse(input, { allowPrototypes: true })`, which retains a `toString` segment (Express 4's default query parser, Express 5's `extended` query parser, and body-parser's `extended` urlencoded parser all set it), `qs.parse(input, { plainObjects: true })`, whose null-prototype elements throw even without a `toString` key (eg, `a[][b]=c`), and `JSON.parse` of a request body, which needs no qs parse option at all. No authentication or user interaction is required. Demonstrated capability: a single request forces an uncaught synchronous `TypeError` in the serialization call. In a naive single-process Node service with no synchronous error boundary, this crashes the process and takes the service offline (availability impact). Under a framework such as Express that traps synchronous handler throws, the plausible outcome is a per-request 500 rather than a full outage; that lower-impact case is noted but not the worst credible supported deployment. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact, no memory unsafety, and no prototype pollution.

## Proof of Concept

`Install qs at the affected version (for example 6.16.0) and run the following script with Node.js. No network setup is required; it demonstrates the throw in isolation.`

```js
var qs = require('qs');

// Source A: qs.parse with allowPrototypes retains the hostile toString segment
qs.stringify(qs.parse('a[0][toString]=x', { allowPrototypes: true }), { arrayFormat: 'comma' });

// Source B: a JSON request body, no qs parse option needed
qs.stringify(JSON.parse('{"a":[{"toString":"x"}]}'), { arrayFormat: 'comma' });

// Also affected: the encodeValuesOnly sub-path
qs.stringify(JSON.parse('{"a":[{"toString":"x"}]}'), { arrayFormat: 'comma', encodeValuesOnly: true });
```

```text
A default-join (allowPrototypes) => THREW: TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value
B default-join (JSON.parse) => THREW: TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value
C encodeValuesOnly path => THREW: TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value
N2 callable toString => NO THROW; output="a=z"
N3 isBuffer vector (CVE-2026-82417) => NO THROW; output="a%5Bconstructor%5D%5BisBuffer%5D=x"
qs version: 6.16.0
```

## Attack Chain

1. **Exposure:** A remote, unauthenticated request reaches an endpoint whose handler eventually serializes attacker-influenced data with `qs.stringify(obj, { arrayFormat: 'comma' })`.
2. **Control:** The attacker supplies data that becomes `{ a: [ { toString: <non-callable value> } ] }`, either via `a[0][toString]=x` parsed with `allowPrototypes`, or via a JSON body `{"a":[{"toString":"x"}]}`.
3. **Path:** In `stringify`, the primitive/buffer guard at `lib/stringify.js:134` is false for an array, so control reaches the comma branch at `lib/stringify.js:149`.
4. **Guard:** On the `encodeValuesOnly` path, the closure `v == null ? v : encoder(v)` at `lib/stringify.js:152-154` passes only `null`/`undefined` through; a non-null object still reaches the encoder. The default path skips that closure entirely and reaches `obj.join(',')` at `lib/stringify.js:156` with no guard at all.
5. **Primitive:** The element is coerced to a string (`Array.prototype.join`, or `String(str)` at `lib/utils.js:292`). `ToPrimitive` skips the non-callable own `toString`, `valueOf` returns the object, and a `TypeError` is thrown.
6. **Result:** The uncaught synchronous exception propagates out of the serialization call, failing the request and, in a service without a synchronous error boundary, crashing the process (denial of service).

## Bypass Evidence

This is a different element type on the code path CVE-2026-8723 (GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26) patched, plus the default comma path, which that fix never covered. CVE-2026-8723 addressed a `TypeError` crash on `null`/`undefined` entries in the comma plus `encodeValuesOnly` path. Its fix (commit 21f80b3) wraps the encoder in `function (v) { return v == null ? v : encoder(v); }`, so it only passes `null` and `undefined` through. A non-null element with a hostile own `toString` fails the `v == null` test, so the encoder still runs and still throws; the encodeValuesOnly case (case C above) throws on the exact fixed code. The default comma path (`encodeValuesOnly` unset, the library default) never entered that fix at all: `git log -S "obj.join(','" -- lib/stringify.js` shows no security fix has ever touched the `obj.join(',')` line, and cases A and B throw with `encodeValuesOnly` unset. The related isBuffer hardening for CVE-2026-82417 (commit e83d321) is a different sink at the `lib/stringify.js:134` guard, which is never entered for the array element; the negative control `{a:{constructor:{isBuffer:'x'}}}` serializes cleanly. Disproof attempts that failed: a `valueOf`-only object does not throw (it serializes to `[object Object]`), confirming the trigger is an element with no callable `toString` (an own non-callable `toString`, or a null-prototype object with no `toString` at all, as `qs.parse` produces under `plainObjects`); nested arrays (`{"a":[[{"toString":"x"}]]}`) throw the same way; a callable `toString` serializes cleanly; and the default (non-comma) array format serializes cleanly, confirming the comma format is required. All positive and negative cases were reproduced on the exact published 6.16.0 artifact.

## Affected Versions

- `Ecosystem: npm`
- `Package: qs`
- `Confirmed affected range: >= 6.7.0, <= 6.16.0`
- `Latest release checked: 6.16.0 (npm latest; git tag v6.16.0)`
- `Fix status: fixed in 6.16.1 (a952e75)`

The `arrayFormat: 'comma'` join sink was introduced in qs 6.7.0, so 6.7.0 is the lower boundary; releases before 6.7.0 lack the sink. No released version fixes this vector, and the latest published release (6.16.0) reproduces the throw, so the closed upper bound `<= 6.16.0` covers every affected release. The `encodeValuesOnly` sub-path was added later, but the default comma-join vector already affects 6.7.0, so 6.7.0 governs the lower boundary.

## Suggested Fix

The comma array serialization must not allow an implicit string coercion of an array element to throw an uncaught exception. Coercion of each comma element should be performed defensively (for example by wrapping the join and per-element encode so that a coercion failure is caught and handled), and this protection must cover both the default `obj.join(',')` path and the `encodeValuesOnly` encoder path, not only the previously patched `null`/`undefined` case. As an interim mitigation without a code change, applications can avoid `arrayFormat: 'comma'` when serializing data derived from untrusted input, sanitize parsed objects (avoid `allowPrototypes`/`plainObjects` on untrusted input and strip unexpected own properties), or wrap `qs.stringify` calls in a synchronous error boundary so a coercion failure cannot crash the process.

Reported by zx (GitHub: @manus-pi).

## Independent report by @Lucidsec

The following was reported separately, after this advisory, and is merged here as a duplicate.

### Summary

In project [qs](https://github.com/ljharb/qs), in versions `>= 6.7.0, <= 6.16.0` (every version that supports `arrayFormat: 'comma'`), `qs.stringify` with `arrayFormat: 'comma'` can throw an uncaught `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` when an array element has a non-callable own `toString`. It is fixed in 6.16.1. Related: CWE-248 and CWE-704.

### Technical Details

`qs.stringify` with `arrayFormat: 'comma'` joins an array at `lib/stringify.js:156` via `obj.join(',')`. An element whose own `toString` is not callable makes `Array.prototype.join` throw. There is no type check and no catch on that path.

A second path exists with `encodeValuesOnly`: at `lib/stringify.js:151-154`, `maybeMap` only skips `v == null`, then `lib/utils.js:292` does `String(str)` and throws the same `TypeError` (this second site exists since v6.11.1; before that, the same input throws at `join`).

Who can trigger: someone who can shape an array element passed to `stringify`. The host must use non-default `arrayFormat: 'comma'`. Default `arrayFormat` `indices` does not fold arrays and is not affected. A parse-then-stringify path also needs `plainObjects: true` (null-prototype elements from `lib/parse.js:200`) or `allowPrototypes: true` (which Express 4's default query parser, Express 5's `extended` query parser, and body-parser's `extended` urlencoded parser all set). Default `qs.parse('a[0][toString]=x')` returns `{}` because the prototype guard drops `toString`. Direct JSON handed to `stringify` can supply `{"a":[{"toString":"x"}]}`.

Cause: the comma fold at `lib/stringify.js:149-156` collapses the array into a single value before the main loop at `lib/stringify.js:172-212`, so `skipNulls` and `strictNullHandling` only ever see the joined value, never individual elements. `isNonNullishPrimitive` / `isBuffer` at `lib/stringify.js:134` inspect the whole value, not each element. A normal object uses `Object.prototype.toString` and becomes `[object Object]`. An own non-callable `toString` is skipped, `valueOf` returns the object, and `join` throws. (The skipped TODO test at `test/stringify.js:684-689` uses a plain `{ b: 1 }` element, which does not throw; it covers the separate question of what comma format should output for object elements, not this crash.) Earlier comma crash fixes did not cover object elements.

### Impact

One small input makes that serialization path throw a synchronous, catchable `TypeError`. Behind a framework error boundary (eg, a synchronous Express handler), the request fails with a 500 and the process survives. In a host with no error boundary (eg, a bare `http.createServer` handler), the uncaught exception exits the process (the client sees `ECONNRESET`). Availability only.

### Proof of Concept

<details>
<summary>Show the proof of concept</summary>

Checked on the latest commit that was checked: `07b1d4d82c8f9301c105ea4b94fa2302cfd6e8b4`. Still present. Demonstrated.

- Payload `{"a":[{"toString":"x"}]}` throws at `lib/stringify.js:156`.
- Baseline `{"a":["x","y"]}` returns 200 with body `a=x%2Cy`.
- A plain object element stringifies to `a=%5Bobject%20Object%5D` and does not throw.
- `encodeValuesOnly: true` throws via `utils.js:292`.
- `plainObjects` parse plus comma throws.

</details>

### Suggested Fix

Before `join`, map elements with the existing primitive check; skip or replace non-primitives so `join` cannot throw. On the `encodeValuesOnly` path, do not send non-primitives into `String()`. Optionally guard `lib/utils.js:292`. Add new regression tests.

title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded automatic PONG buffering
desc:
### Impact

undici's WebSocket client (including Node.js's bundled `globalThis.WebSocket`) can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised WebSocket server. For every PING frame received, the receiver automatically writes a PONG response to the socket and ignores the `false` return value from `socket.write()`, which is a backpressure signal, so a server that streams small PING frames while never reading the client's PONGs makes the outbound write queue and heap grow without bound until the Node.js process runs out of memory and terminates. The attack is remote and unauthenticated, needs only a normal WebSocket connection, and is asymmetric: small inbound PINGs produce a much larger retained outbound queue. Availability is the only impact. undici 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected; the WebSocket client was introduced in 5.15.0.

### Patches

Upgrade to `6.29.1`, `7.30.1`, or `8.12.2`, which pause WebSocket frame parsing when the automatic PONG response hits socket backpressure and resume on drain, bounding the outbound queue.

### Workarounds

None.

title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via failed HTTP/2 handshake
desc:
### Impact

undici's experimental WebSocket client (enabled by default via `allowH2: true`) crashes the Node.js process when it connects to a malicious server over HTTP/2. If the server answers the WebSocket upgrade with a response that fails handshake validation, undici aborts the request, but the abort is a no-op because the request is already marked completed, so the underlying `ClientHttp2Stream` is left open with no error listener. When the server then destroys the connection, the orphaned stream emits an unhandled `error` and the process exits. A remote, unauthenticated server can therefore deny service to any client that opens a WebSocket to it over HTTP/2. undici 8.11.0 and 8.11.1 are affected; the regression was introduced in 8.11.0.

### Patches

Upgrade to `8.11.2`.

### Workarounds

Set `allowH2: false` to disable HTTP/2 for WebSocket connections, or avoid opening WebSocket connections to untrusted servers, until upgrading.

title: undici vulnerable to cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via cross-origin redirects
desc:
### Impact

When an originless `Agent` composes the redirect and cache interceptors as `compose(redirect(), cache())` with a shared cache (`type: 'shared'`), the cache builds its key from the original request URL before the redirect handler changes the origin. The response produced after a redirect is then stored under the original key, even when the redirect crossed to a different origin.

An attacker who controls the target of a redirect from a trusted URL can have their response cached under that trusted URL. A later caller requesting the trusted URL receives the attacker's body from the shared cache without either origin being contacted, allowing persistent cache poisoning. The same key confusion also discloses private data: when an authenticated request returns a `private, no-store` redirect to a user-specific resource, the final response is stored under the original URL and can be served to a later unauthenticated caller.

The cache interceptor was introduced in undici 7.0.0, and all 7.x and 8.x releases before the patched versions are affected. Applications are affected only when an originless `Agent`, a shared `MemoryCacheStore` or `SqliteCacheStore`, and the composition `compose(redirect(), cache())` are all used. Origin-bound `Client` and `Pool` dispatchers, and the reverse composition `compose(cache(), redirect())`, are not affected.

### Patches

Upgrade to `7.30.1` or `8.12.2`. Before storing a response, undici now verifies that the origin that produced it still matches the cache key, and preserves each redirect hop's cache-control policy, so cross-origin redirect responses and responses behind a `no-store` or `private` hop are no longer cached under the original key.

### Workarounds

Compose the interceptors as `compose(cache(), redirect())`, use per-origin dispatchers and cache stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable requests.

title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
desc:
### Description

`Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as `[[[[...]]]]`, exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.

Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes `#[MapRequestPayload]` when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict `acceptFormat`: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.

### Resolution

The inline lexer now enters and leaves the same nesting level as the rest of the parser, so nested inline collections are bounded by `maxNestingLevel`, and the parser raises a `ParseException` beyond it.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/2a8bf9c58d862b0c76a35ce288d1ba6a27223aad) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

We would like to thank Nicolas Grekas for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

### References

- Fix: [#65688](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/pull/65688)

title: undici vulnerable to TLS certificate validation bypass via dropped tls options in Agent
desc:
### Impact

undici's `Agent` passes its constructor options through a JSON-based deep clone (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`) before forwarding them to each per-origin `Pool`. JSON cannot represent functions, so a caller-supplied `tls` option containing a `checkServerIdentity` callback is silently dropped before it reaches the TLS layer. As a result, a TLS peer whose certificate a custom `checkServerIdentity` was written to reject, but which passes Node's default hostname and chain checks, is silently accepted when the request is made through `Agent`. Because `Agent` is the default dispatcher behind `request`, `fetch`, and `setGlobalDispatcher`, this is the path most applications use. `EnvHttpProxyAgent` is also affected on its direct and `NO_PROXY` routes, which delegate to an internal `Agent`.

Only applications that pass a function-valued `tls` option (such as a custom `checkServerIdentity` for certificate or public-key pinning) are affected. Passing the same options through `connect` is not affected. This is the `Agent` counterpart of the `BalancedPool` certificate validation bypass fixed in CVE-2026-84961.

### Patches

Upgrade to undici `6.29.1`, `7.30.1`, or `8.12.2`. `Agent` now preserves the `tls` option outside the JSON clone, so custom TLS verification callbacks are forwarded to each origin unchanged.

### Workarounds

Pass the TLS options through `connect` instead of `tls`. For proxied `EnvHttpProxyAgent` destinations, use `requestTls` / `proxyTls`.

title: PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading
desc: ## Summary PhpSpreadsheet's `Worksheet\Drawing::setPath()` validates an external-image URL against an operator-supplied `isWhitelisted` callback **once**, on the initial URL only, then fetches it with `file_get_contents()` using a stream context that does **not** set `follow_location => 0`. A whitelisted host that returns an HTTP `302 Location:` redirect to an internal target is therefore followed by PHP's HTTP wrapper (default `follow_location=1`, `max_redirects=20`) with **no re-validation of the redirect hop** — defeating the whitelist and yielding a blind SSRF from the server. This is an unfixed variant of CVE-2026-59931 (GHSA-6hq5-7373-42rg, the WEBSERVICE redirect-whitelist-bypass): the `follow_location => 0` fix (commit `7ef7b25e`) was applied ONLY to `Calculation/Web/Service.php`; `Worksheet/Drawing.php` was never touched. ## Root Cause `src/PhpSpreadsheet/Worksheet/Drawing.php`: - Scheme allowlist at `:125` (`/^(http|https|file|ftp|s3):/`) permits `http`/`https` (the redirect-following schemes) and runs on the initial URL only. - Opt-in gate `if (!$allowExternal)` at `:128` (requires `setAllowExternalImages(true)`; default `false`, `BaseReader.php:55`). - Whitelist check `if ($isWhitelisted !== null && !$isWhitelisted($path))` at `:131` — validates the INITIAL URL only; never re-applied after a redirect. - Stream context built at `:140-152` sets `user_agent` + `header` (+ `ssl.crypto_method` for https) but **omits `follow_location`**. `git grep follow_location` on tag 5.9.0 yields a single hit — `Service.php:45` (the CVE-2026-59931 fix) — confirming it was never added to `Drawing.php`. - Sink `file_get_contents($path, false, $ctx)` at `:154`. ## Impact Blind SSRF from the server: reach and trigger internal GET-driven endpoints, coarse internal reachability/port probing, and reach cloud-metadata endpoints. The fetched body is written to a temp file, checked with `isImage()` (mime `image/*`, or `application/octet-stream` with `bin`/`emf` extension), only image dimensions are stored, and the temp file is `unlink`ed — so the response body is **not** exfiltrated (non-image responses fail `isImage()`). This is a blind GET primitive, not full response read. ## Proof of Concept 1. Attacker server `https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png` returns `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`. 2. `evil.xlsx` with `xl/drawings/_rels/drawing1.xml.rels`: ``. 3. Victim: `$r = new Xlsx(); $r->setAllowExternalImages(true)->setIsWhitelisted(fn($p)=>str_contains($p,'trusted-whitelisted.example')); $r->load('evil.xlsx');` -> the server-side GET is forced to the internal target despite the whitelist. HTML-reader variant: `` loaded via `Reader\Html` (`Html.php:1237`) with the same reader settings. ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: crafted `evil.xlsx`, `xl/drawings/_rels/*.rels` `TargetMode="External"`, `Target="https://trusted.example/redir.png"` (whitelisted host). Guard: none (legal external-image relationship). Bypass proof: Target stored verbatim -> `$url` at `Reader/Xlsx.php:1544`. 2. Config: victim loads with `setAllowExternalImages(true)->setIsWhitelisted($cb)` where `$cb` allows `trusted.example`. Guard: `Drawing.php:128` opt-in (satisfied) + `:131` whitelist. Bypass proof: initial URL is whitelisted -> returns true; check runs once on `$path`. 3. Fetch/redirect: `file_get_contents` (`:154`) GETs the URL; whitelisted host returns `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/...`. Guard: stream context (`:140-152`). Bypass proof: no `follow_location` key -> PHP follows the redirect (default `follow_location=1`, `max_redirects=20`) with no re-validation. 4. Impact: server issues a blind GET to the internal target (body temp-filed, `isImage()`-checked, dimensions stored, temp file unlinked — body not exfiltrated). ## Bypass Evidence - `git grep follow_location 5.9.0 -- src/` -> single hit at `Service.php:45`; `Drawing.php` has none. - CVE-2026-59931's own regression harness (`ServerTest.php` + `redirect.php`: a whitelisted host 302-redirects to `direct.php`; only after `follow_location => 0` does the fetch stop following it) demonstrates the exact behavior. That fix is present in `Service.php` and absent in `Drawing.php`. - `git grep isWhitelisted 5.9.0 -- src/` confirms the callback is applied only at `Drawing.php:131` (initial `$path`), never after the redirect. ## Affected Versions `>= 5.5.0, <= 5.9.0`. The `isWhitelisted` control being bypassed was introduced in 5.5.0 (commit `50a7552f`); present and unfixed on the latest release (5.9.0) and on HEAD (`05e99ebf`). No post-release fix to `Drawing.php`. ## Suggested Fix Add `'follow_location' => 0` (and/or `'max_redirects' => 0`) to `$ctxArray['http']` in `Drawing::setPath()` (`:140-148`), mirroring the CVE-2026-59931 fix at `Service.php:45`; alternatively follow redirects manually and re-run `$isWhitelisted` on each hop. --- Reported by **zx (Jace)** — GitHub: @manus-use

title: PhpSpreadsheet ODS Reader: Unbounded number-rows-repeated → CPU & Memory Exhaustion (DoS)
desc:
## Summary

When PhpSpreadsheet loads an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (`.ods`), `Ods::processTableRow()`
reads the `table:number-rows-repeated` attribute of a `<table:table-row>` with an unchecked 
`(int)` cast, then materialises one cell per repeated row. This value is **completely unbounded**, 
so a **single ~1.4 KB file** can instruct the reader to create up to **millions of cells**, 
exhausting memory (fatal OOM). No authentication, no special configuration, and the default read 
filter are required - any application that loads a user-supplied `.ods` is affected.

---

## Affected versions

The `number-rows-repeated` expansion has existed in the ODS reader since its inception
(pre-dating the current release branches), so all maintained lines are affected.

| Branch | Affected |
|--------|----------|
| 1.x    | ≤ 1.30.6 |
| 2.0–2.1 | ≤ 2.1.18 |
| 2.2–2.4 | ≤ 2.4.7 |
| 3.x    | ≤ 3.10.7 |
| 4.x–5.x | ≤ 5.9.0 (latest) |

---

## Root cause (source → sink)

`src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php`:

```php
// line 816 — row repeat, unchecked (int) cast
$rowRepeats = (int) $childNode->getAttributeNS($tableNs, 'number-rows-repeated');
...
// line 1151 — row materialisation loop: NO upper bound
for ($rowAdjust = 0; $rowAdjust < $rowRepeats; ++$rowAdjust) {
    $rID = $rowID + $rowAdjust;
    $cell = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell($columnID . $rID);  // allocates a Cell
    $cell->setValueExplicit($dataValue, $type);
    // ... no bounds check on $rowAdjust or $rID ...
}
```

**Why columns are NOT vulnerable (already bounded):**

The column-header loop at line 1326 shows the correct pattern with bounds checking:

```php
// line 1326 (processTableColumnHeader): BOUNDED correctly
for ($rowRepeats2 = $rowRepeats; $rowRepeats2 > 0 && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT; --$rowRepeats2) {
    // HAS BOUNDS CHECK: && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT
}
```

Additionally, the cell-data column loop at line 1141 calls `getCell()` which throws exception 
at `Coordinate.php:448` when column exceeds `MAX_COLUMN_INT` (XFD / 16,384):

```php
// Coordinate.php line 448
if ($columnIndex > self::MAX_COLUMN_INT) {
    throw new Exception('Column string index can not be beyond XFD');
}
```

**Result:** Columns are capped at 16,384. Only rows are unbounded.

---

## Impact

**Memory exhaustion (single valued cell, repeated many rows):**  
A non-null cell value with a huge `number-rows-repeated` attribute materialises millions of 
`Cell` objects → PHP fatal `Allowed memory size ... exhausted`.

**Example:**
- Payload: `<table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000">` (5 million rows)
- File size: 1.4 KB
- Memory consumed: ~256 MB (one Cell object per row)
- Result: OOM at default memory limit

---

## Reproduction

**Vulnerable payload (causes OOM):**

```xml
<table:table table:name="Sheet1">
 <table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000">
  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>
 </table:table-row>
</table:table>
```

**Not vulnerable (for reference - throws exception):**

```xml
<table:table table:name="Sheet1">
 <table:table-row>
  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1"
      table:number-columns-repeated="1000000000">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>
 </table:table-row>
</table:table>
```

This column-repeat example throws `Column string index can not be beyond XFD` exception
(bounded defense, already in place).

title: snappy-java: Unbounded memory allocation from attacker-declared uncompressed lengtha
desc:
### Impact
Several decompression paths in snappy-java allocate an output buffer sized by the uncompressed length declared in the first bytes of the compressed data, before decompressing or validating it. A few bytes of crafted input can therefore force an allocation of up to 2 GB, causing `OutOfMemoryError` (denial of service), or a `NegativeArraySizeException` for declared lengths of 2^31 or more.

Affected entry points include `Snappy.uncompress(byte[])`, `Snappy.uncompressString`, the `Snappy.uncompress*Array` methods, `SnappyInputStream`, and `SnappyFramedInputStream`. The `maxChunkSize` limit added for CVE-2023-43642 bounds only the compressed chunk length, so it does not prevent this.

### Patches
Fixed in 1.1.10.9 (#739). `Snappy.uncompressedLength()` now rejects negative declared lengths, and lengths larger than any valid Snappy stream of the given size can produce. The densest Snappy element expands 3 bytes to 64, so the limit is 64/3 of the compressed size. Allocations are therefore proportional to the input actually received.

### Workarounds
Before decompressing untrusted data, check that `Snappy.uncompressedLength(input)` is within an application-specific limit.

title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header
desc:
### Description

`HeaderUtils::split()` parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a `(?<!\s)` lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. `HeaderBag` calls it for the `Cache-Control` header whenever a `Request` is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.

A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, `preg_match_all()` gives up at `pcre.backtrack_limit` and `split()` returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.

### Resolution

The pattern now consumes whitespace only when more of the value follows it, so a value can no longer end on whitespace, nothing has to be given back, and every quantifier is possessive. The first release of this fix broke splitting on a whitespace separator: `HeaderUtils::split('foo bar', ' ')` returned a single value in 6.4.46 to 6.4.47, 7.4.19 to 7.4.20 and 8.1.7 to 8.1.8. Whitespace characters used as separators are now left out of the whitespace branch, which 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9 contain.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/343a1772ce6ac03e48b228d2d7168d19750e3f36) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

Symfony would like to thank [r3verii](https://github.com/r3verii) for reporting the issue and Nicolas Grekas for providing the fix.

Symfony would also like to thank [Bruno Dias](https://github.com/cx-bruno-dias) from Checkmarx for his help getting a CVE assigned.

title: MongoDB Python Driver: Out-of-bounds read in BSON decoding via a malformed Regex element
desc:
### Impact
The C extension's BSON decoder scans a Regex element's pattern and flags strings with strlen before checking the document's remaining length, so a crafted truncated Regex element can read past the end of the caller's buffer. bson.decode and bson.decode_all accept mmap and array buffers, which carry no NUL sentinel; the read can cross into unmapped memory and kill the process with an uncatchable SIGSEGV. Any application decoding untrusted BSON from such buffers is affected — impact is availability only, since the out-of-bounds bytes are never returned as content. NUL-terminated buffers (bytes, bytearray) raise `InvalidBSON` at worst; the driver's own transport and pure-Python installs are not affected. All releases through 4.18.2 are affected when the C extension is loaded.

### Patches
Fixed in PyMongo 4.18.3. Malformed Regex elements now raise InvalidBSON on every accepted buffer type; valid documents decode unchanged.

###  Workarounds
Decode untrusted BSON only from NUL-terminated buffers — bytes or bytearray — and copy mmap input first, e.g. bytes(mm[:size]).

title: The 3D Viewer for Nextcloud is a comprehensive 3D model viewer application for Nextcloud that supports multiple 3D file formats.
desc: The 3D Viewer for Nextcloud is a comprehensive 3D model viewer application for Nextcloud that supports multiple 3D file formats. In versions 1.7.9 through 3.3.1, the app's public file endpoint performed no share authorization. Anyone who knows a share token could read the shared file's contents even when the link share was protected by a password. `PublicFileController` extended `OCP\AppFramework\Controller` and marked its routes `#[PublicPage]`. Nextcloud only enforces share passwords through `PublicShareMiddleware`, which returns early for any controller that is not an `OCP\AppFramework\PublicShareController` instance — so no password, expiry, or share-type check ran for these routes. `ShareFileService::loadLinkShare()` compounded this by treating any token that `getShareByToken()` matched as authorised. A share token is the part of the URL that people paste into chats, emails, and tickets. Password protection exists precisely for the case where holding the token should not by itself grant access, and that guarantee did not hold. Requests to `GET /ocs/v2.php/apps/threedviewer/public/file/{token}/{fileId}` returned `200` with the full file body for password-protected shares, with no password and no session. Nextcloud's own share page correctly redirected such requests to the password prompt. Scope is limited to files in the formats this app handles (STL, GLB/glTF, OBJ, STEP, IFC, and the other supported 3D types). Non-3D files in the same share are unaffected. Expired shares returned `500` rather than leaking contents. This issue is fixed in 3.3.2. `PublicFileController` now extends `PublicShareController` and implements `isValidToken()`, `isPasswordProtected()`, and `getPasswordHash()`, delegating password and token validation to the framework and gaining brute-force throttling. `ShareFileService::findValidLinkShare()` additionally rejects share types other than link and email, rejects expired shares, and treats a `ShareNotFound` from the share manager as "no share" instead of letting it surface as a 500. As a workaround, disable the 3D Viewer app (`occ app:disable threedviewer`), or avoid relying on passwords to protect link shares that contain 3D model files, until you can upgrade.

privileges and execute arbitrary operating-system commands on the affected
device.

accessible.









Successful
exploitation may allow an unauthenticated attacker on the same local area
network to execute arbitrary system commands with root privileges.

Because the interface lacks an effective attempt counter or lockout mechanism and uses a predictable verification-code generation process, an attacker may obtain or brute-force the code and reset the administrator password. 





Successful exploitation may allow an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to reset the administrator password and subsequently access privileged device-management functions.

extract the cryptographic material from the firmware and use it to decrypt the
backup. 









Successful
exploitation may disclose sensitive configuration information contained in a
backup file, including administrator passwords and Wi-Fi credentials.
